title: Contain Linux guest job descendants across setsid and process-group escape
description: Prerequisite of97341ad5: the root Linux GUARD must own kernel-enforced lifetime of the job and every descendant, including setsid/setpgid/double-fork escape, before its completion EOF/status is observable. Deliver within guest-supervisor.py and a new scripts/tests/local-runner-guard.test.mjs; retain the private GUARD interface: '+' only once the job starts, start-pipe EOF after job/descendant teardown, and outer guard waitpid status mirrors the actual job exit/signal. A private PID namespace with a trusted namespace-init shim is the preferred bounded mechanism: outer root guard creates namespace before any watcher thread/forked job; inner init waits the job, transmits its trusted raw wait status over a private close-on-exec pipe, and exits so the kernel kills remaining namespace descendants. Outer guard reaps init before reflecting the job status; do not turn a signal into a successful exit. Existing life-pipe EOF/group kill must still terminate init from its ancestor namespace, killing escaped descendants even after supervisor SIGKILL. Missing kernel capability/API or malformed/incomplete status must fail closed, never launch uncontained or fabricate success. Production main is root-only Linux; preserve explicitly non-certifying non-root POSIX import fixtures without granting a CLI/env bypass. Architect must validate exact integration and sizing; no cgroup/UID/name-wide process sweep. Root Linux unprivileged-userns probe already confirmed nested PID-init exit kills a setsid descendant and preserves separately conveyed job exit7 on this host; URL https://www.man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/pid_namespaces.7.html. Do NOT change pump/host EOF or public framing here: parent owns them and the normal-completion group fallback. Test real kernel namespace behavior in a dedicated child-owned user namespace where supported, plus failure injection, exit0/nonzero/signals, open/closed output, supervisor death, descriptor cleanup and sibling sentinel survival. Full gate from external full snapshot: node --test scripts/tests/local-runner*.test.mjs && (cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test). R13 owns native certification against the new supervisor hash; no verified-local claim.
definitionOfDone: Root Linux GUARD cannot start a job without its owned kernel descendant boundary; unavailable setup fails closed with no successful observation.
Normal completion and supervisor death kill setsid/setpgid/double-fork descendants before completion EOF; real job code/signal remains intact, with owned-process tests.
Private '+', completion EOF and waitpid-status contract remains usable by relay/run_install; existing guards and full external runner+daemon regression pass.
No host-wide/name/UID kill, process scan-to-kill race, credential leak, CLI/env bypass or native certification claim.
